gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen her face when she heard the news!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have seen' emphasizes how remarkable something was: should have.

gaps.sentence: Her car is not in the car park and her office light is off, so she ___ home.
gaps.hint: a confident conclusion about the past
gaps.explanation: A confident conclusion about the past uses 'must have' plus the participle: must have gone.

gaps.sentence: When I was a child, I ___ stay up late on New Year's Eve.
gaps.hint: permission that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Was allowed to' expresses past permission; 'could' is also possible: was allowed to.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have brought a present, but it was kind of her anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' plus the participle means the action happened but was unnecessary: needn't have brought.

gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.

gaps.sentence: Nobody ___ have predicted that result — it shocked everyone.
gaps.hint: it was impossible at that time
gaps.explanation: 'Could have' in negatives means it was not possible: could have predicted.

gaps.sentence: When the lift broke, I ___ walk up ten flights of stairs.
gaps.hint: necessity created by a past event
gaps.explanation: 'Had to' expresses past necessity: had to walk.
